strings.name: Sophie Wilson
strings.summary: Wilson helped design Acorn computers and the BBC Micro, wrote BBC BASIC and co-designed ARM with Steve Furber. Its reduced instruction set and low power needs later suited mobile devices. She subsequently developed FirePath and continued chip work at Broadcom through Element14. A transgender woman, she is also a prominent figure in computing history; these achievements form part of sustained work by many teams.

strings.influence.rationale: Helped design ARM’s instruction set and early personal computers, influencing low-power computing and global mobile-device architectures.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied computer science at Selwyn College, Cambridge, from 1976 to 1979.
strings.highlights.h1.title: BBC Micro and BBC BASIC
strings.highlights.h1.text: Helped design the prototype and system, writing its BASIC interpreter for educational and home users.
strings.highlights.h2.title: ARM and FirePath
strings.highlights.h2.text: Designed ARM with Furber and later developed FirePath for broadband equipment.
strings.timeline.t1.title: ARM’s fortieth anniversary
strings.timeline.t1.text: A Science Museum feature reviewed her work and four decades of ARM processors.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Elected Royal Society Fellow
strings.timeline.t2.text: Her computer and processor design work was recognized by election to the Society.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Computer History Museum Fellow
strings.timeline.t3.text: Honored for joint contributions with Furber to the BBC Micro and ARM architecture.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joined Broadcom
strings.timeline.t4.text: Continued processor and system-on-chip design after Broadcom acquired Element14.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Developed FirePath and cofounded Element14
strings.timeline.t5.text: Established the company with partners to apply FirePath to ADSL broadband.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First ARM silicon
strings.timeline.t6.text: The processor co-designed with Furber reached silicon, underpinning later architectural development.
strings.timeline.t7.title: BBC Micro project
strings.timeline.t7.text: Worked with Acorn’s team on a rapid prototype and developed BBC BASIC and system software.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Entered Cambridge
strings.timeline.t8.text: Began computer-science studies at Selwyn, moving through electronics projects into commercial computer design.
